newsitem.title: UK: Diana says sons want her to quit Britain - papers.
newsitem.headline: Diana says sons want her to quit Britain - papers.

text.p: Princess Diana told journalists and photographers following her on her luxury holiday on the French Riviera that her sons want her to leave Britain for a quieter life, newspapers reported on Tuesday.
The princess, who interrupted her holiday at the villa of luxury store owner Mohammed Al Fayed to speak to them from a motorboat, also promised to reveal "a big surprise" in the next two weeks.
"My boys are urging me continually to leave the country. They say it is the only way," the Mirror newspaper quoted her as saying.

"Maybe that's what I should do. They want me to live abroad. I sit in London all the time and I am abused and followed wherever I go. Now I am being forced to move from here," the princess, tanned and trim in a swimsuit, added.
The top selling Sun newspaper said Diana refused to reveal any further details about her promised surprise.
"I am going to make an announcement in two weeks that is going to put an end to all this. And boy, will you be surprised," she said.

The speedboat trip to the waiting press corps and her candid conversation was an extraordinary move by the princess, who has been criticised for sharing a holiday with Al Fayed, the owner of top London department store Harrods, and the man blamed by opposition Conservative MPs for their disastrous showing in the May 1 election.

Al Fayed was at the centre of the sleaze scandal that crushed the previous Conservative government after he revealed to newspapers that he had paid several MPs thousands of pounds (dollars) to ask questions in parliament on his behalf.
Photographs splashed across newspapers on Monday showing the princess and the Egyptian-born tycoon arm-in-arm on his yacht sparked criticism from politicians and right-wing editorial writers.
"Mr Fayed is not the sort of person in whose debt a public figure such as the princess should knowingly place herself and her sons," said the Daily Telegraph.
Diana, who is with her two sons William, 15, and Harry, 12, said she was hurt by the criticism and uproar her holiday had caused in Britain.
"Mr Fayed was my father's best friend. I have known him for 10 years. Anyway, to be strictly correct, I am here with his wife," he told the journalists.
